new_packages.proposed_label: מַחֲשָׁבָה וּמְצִיאוּת — זֶהוּת הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה עִם הַפֹּעַל
new_packages.proposed_label_en: Thought and Reality — The Identity of Mental and Physical
new_packages.condition: Requires adding at least 3 bechina edges to torahData.js for reference 193. The minimum cluster to qualify as a new independent domain is: (1) מחשבה ↔ מציאות בפועל, (2) מיתה בפועל ↔ צער המיתה במחשבה, (3) מחשבה תקיפה ↔ ביטול כל ההרגשות. These three edges yield a 5-node cluster: {מחשבה, מציאות בפועל, מיתה בפועל, צער המיתה במחשבה, ביטול כל ההרגשות}.
new_packages.justification: This cluster constitutes a genuine independent conceptual domain: the ontological identity of thought with physical reality. This is not a standard ethical or mystical domain (like תורה, תפלה, or יראה) already well-represented in the dataset. The teaching's core insight — that fully-intensified thought (מחשבה) and physical actuality share the same essential nature — is an epistemological/ontological teaching unique in its formulation among the Torahs. The five concepts all express this same essential nature from different angles: מחשבה is the mental pole, מציאות בפועל is the physical pole, and the three bridge-concepts (מיתה בפועל / צער המיתה / ביטול ההרגשות) articulate the specific conditions under which the identity holds. This is not a sub-domain of an existing package in the dataset — it stands alone as a new domain of discourse about the nature of thought and its relation to reality.
new_packages.domain_independence: The domain of 'thought-reality identity' does not appear as an established package in other Torahs. While מחשבה appears as a node in many Torahs, it is typically in a different role (e.g., evil thoughts, the domain of divine thought, thought as preparation for prayer). The specific claim that thought and physical experience are ontologically identical — illustrated through the experience of martyrdom-pain — is unique to Torah #193's formulation and justifies treating this as a new independent domain.

new_packages.condition: Requires adding at least 3 bechina edges to torahData.js for reference 193. The minimum cluster: (1) מסירת נפש ↔ קידוש השם, (2) קריאת שמע ↔ ארבע מיתות בית דין, (3) מסירת נפש ↔ קריאת שמע.
new_packages.justification: The Shema-martyrdom cluster is a tight, coherent 4-node domain: the act of reciting Shema, the acceptance of martyrdom, the four legal forms of death, and the sanctification of God's name are all identified as expressions of the same essential spiritual reality in this Torah. Rabbi Akiva's practice — accepting all four court deaths during Shema — is presented not as a three-step causal sequence but as a single unified act viewed through ritual, legal, and devotional lenses simultaneously. The domain is clearly good-polarity: it represents the highest peak of holiness, the complete surrender of self to God's name.
new_packages.domain_independence: While מסירת נפש and קידוש השם appear in other Torahs, their specific identification with קריאת שמע and ארבע מיתות בית דין — mediated by the thought-power mechanism — is particular to Torah #193. The bechina within this package is the equation of the three formal modes (ritual/legal/devotional) of the same act, which is a domain-specific structural claim.

observations: Torah #193 currently has zero bechina edges in torahData.js, so the 3+ node threshold for algorithmically proposing new packages cannot be met from the dataset alone. However, the source text is conceptually rich enough to yield two coherent independent domains once the missing bechina edges are added. The two proposed new packages stand in an eitza relationship to each other: Package 1 (thought = reality, neutral) is the mechanism that ENABLES Package 2 (martyrdom = Shema, good). This eitza flow is the Torah's main argument. Neither package is a subset of the other, and their independence is clear: Package 1 discusses the universal phenomenon of thought-power (applicable to both wealth and martyrdom), while Package 2 is the specific holy application. No evil-mirror package is present in Torah #193 — the text does not develop a negative counterpart to either thought-power or martyrdom. The only implicit negative is the closing warning (one must stop before the soul actually departs), which is a practical eitza caveat rather than an evil-domain package.
